# {{ a.name }}

> Bioinformatics scientist at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia building computational and machine learning methods for clinical genomics and cancer immunogenomics. Co-first author of papers in Nature Cancer (2025) and Cancer Cell (2024).

This file summarizes {{ site.url }} for AI assistants. The pages below are plain HTML and may be read directly.

## About

{{ a.name }} (publishes as Jammihal T or Jammihal TR) is a {{ a.title }} in the Division of Genomic Diagnostics at the {{ a.affiliation }}, {{ a.location }}, developing and clinically translating methods for finding structural and copy-number variants in genome sequencing data to help diagnose rare pediatric disease. Current work: structural variant detection and machine learning-based variant triage in clinical genome sequencing.

Earlier roles: cancer immunogenomics at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (2020–2022) and MD Anderson Cancer Center (2022–2023), studying why some patients respond exceptionally well to immunotherapy; computational biology co-op at Novartis Institutes for BioMedical Research (2019–2020).

Education: Master of Biotechnology, The Pennsylvania State University (2020); M.Tech and B.Tech in Biological Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Madras (2017).

## Research areas

- Clinical genomics for rare pediatric disease: structural and copy-number variant detection in clinical genome sequencing
- Cancer immunogenomics: clonal neoantigens, tertiary lymphoid structures and molecular subtypes as biomarkers of immunotherapy response
- Machine learning for genomic interpretation: deep learning and AutoML for human-in-the-loop variant triage
